samples.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!



Role Overview:

As a Machine Learning Engineer specializing in pretraining data, you will play a pivotal role in developing the data pipeline that underpins Cohere’s advanced language models. In this role, you will conduct data ablations to evaluate data quality and construct pre-training data mixtures to enhance model performance. By combining research and engineering, you will bridge the gap between raw data and cutting-edge AI models, directly contributing to improvements in critical training metrics like throughput and accelerator utilization.

Your work will be essential to Cohere’s mission of delivering efficient and reliable language understanding and generation capabilities, driving innovation in natural language processing. If you are passionate about transforming data into the foundation of AI systems, this role offers a unique opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

Please Note: We have offices in London, Paris, Toronto, San Francisco and New York but also embrace being remote-friendly! There are no restrictions on where you can be located for this role between EST and EU.




Key Responsibilities:

 - Conduct data ablations to assess data quality and experiment with data mixtures to enhance model performance.

 - Develop robust data modeling techniques to ensure datasets are structured and formatted for optimal training efficiency.

 - Research and implement innovative data curation methods, leveraging Cohere’s infrastructure to drive advancements in natural language processing.

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including researchers and engineers, to ensure data pipelines meet the demands of cutting-edge language models.



Qualifications:

 - Strong software engineering skills, with proficiency in Python and experience building data pipelines.

 - Familiarity with curriculum learning, data mixing and data attribution.

 - Familiarity with data processing frameworks such as Apache Spark, Apache Beam, Pandas, or similar tools.

 - Experience working with large-scale datasets, including web data, code data, and multilingual corpora.

 - Knowledge of data quality assessment techniques and experimentation with data mixtures.

 - A passion for bridging research and engineering to solve complex data-related challenges in AI model training.

Bonus: paper at top-tier venues (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AIStats, MLSys, JMLR, AAAI, Nature, COLING, ACL, EMNLP).



Working Location:
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.






FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

What We Do

Wagmo is a modern pet healthcare company built around how pet parents actually care for their pets. We partner with employers to provide a complete approach to pet and pet-parent wellbeing, from preventive wellness plans and emergency coverage to 24/7 pet telehealth guidance. Our purpose is to unlock every pet parent's potential to provide extraordinary care, and we do it by bringing the same intentionality to pet benefits that the best employers bring to human healthcare. Founded in 2017 and female-founded, Wagmo is headquartered in New York City and trusted by leading employers nationwide.



What's Important to Us

Our mission shapes everything we build and how we work together. We take fearless ownership of outcomes, collaborate with radical candor, and are always driven by the customers and pet parents who trust us. We think critically, follow through relentlessly, and find the extra 10% that turns good work into exceptional work. We keep it weird because the obvious answer is rarely the most interesting one. Our values aren't aspirational. We interview for them and hold each other accountable to them. If what you've read so far resonates with you and you want to be part of a team where every person makes the company meaningfully better, we'd love to hear from you.



About The Role

You'll own the day-to-day performance and evolution of Wagmo's Support and Claims automation. You'll monitor production AI workflows, tune prompts and logic, and keep automation accurate, useful, and personal as we scale.


You'll also improve the tools our team uses every day, including Zendesk routing, triggers, macros, agent assist, and related workflows.


In the near term, you'll move our channel bots from generic help content to personalized responses powered by live customer data. Longer term, you'll partner closely with Engineering to expand Wagmo's custom AI capabilities and improve the speed, accuracy, and quality of our customer experience.


You don't need to be a software engineer. You do need to be comfortable working in technical tools, evaluation platforms like LangSmith, and APIs, and know when to solve something yourself versus bring in Engineering.



Location: This is a remote role open to candidates based in the United States, with a preference for candidates working in Eastern Time.



Core Responsibilities

 - Own day-to-day performance of AI and automation across Support and Claims.

 - Monitor accuracy, failure patterns, and performance changes, then tune prompts and workflows to improve results.

 - Build and maintain evaluations, including test cases, golden datasets, and regression checks.

 - Test changes before production with Claims and Support SMEs.

 - Rebuild generic channel bots to use live APIs for more personalized interactions.

 - Track and report automation performance, including automation rate, accuracy, escalation, and BSAT.

 - Partner with Engineering on work that requires deeper technical build.
   
   

What You'll Need To Be Successful

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience building and improving AI-powered workflows and automation, ideally in customer service or operations.

 - Strong understanding of prompt design, workflow logic, AI evaluation, and failure analysis, including structured testing or quality review.

 - Extensive experience with Zendesk AI or a comparable service platform, with comfort working with APIs and structured data. Coding experience is helpful, not required.

 - Strong diagnostic judgment, with the ability to trace performance issues to root causes and determine the right next action.

 - Ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams, translating operational needs into practical AI solutions.

 - Strong customer communication instincts and a demonstrated commitment to staying current on emerging AI tools, techniques, and applications.



Why Consider This Role?

 - Pet spending in the U.S. has reached $200 billion and the category is still early in its lifecycle. Wagmo is building the platform to lead it. This is a rare chance to join at a moment when the work you do today shapes what the industry looks like tomorrow.

 - Wagmo is a female-founded, Inc. 5000 recognized company where performance matters more than pedigree. We are growing fast, building something that matters, and there is real ownership equity in that journey.

 - The team is exceptionally smart, curious, and kind, led by transparent and low-ego leadership. We take the work seriously and never take ourselves too seriously. This is not a traditional 9-to-5 job. It asks for real dedication and impact, and gives you genuine flexibility and autonomy in return.



Key Benefits

• Comprehensive health, vision, and dental coverage

• HSA/FSA

• 401(k) retirement planning with employer matching

• Unlimited paid time off

• Annual company holidays

• Additional company-wide recharge days off

• 12 weeks parental leave for eligible employees

• Company paid Wagmo pet wellness and insurance plans

• Annual fully-paid company-wide retreat

WRITER is the AI platform built for the world’s most ambitious marketing and revenue teams, bringing the frontier of AI to the people who drive enterprise growth. With WRITER, autonomous agents work across the buyer journey, continuously executing on market signals and enterprise intelligence to grow revenue faster. Every agent action and asset is grounded in trust, built on an Enterprise Brain that unites brand, product, and company knowledge with fiduciary-grade governance and compliance. 



Fortune 500 companies are transforming how they go to market with WRITER, including 3 of the top 5 US banks, 2 of the 5 largest global CPG conglomerates, and 4 of the top 5 US healthcare insurers. Learn more at WRITER.com http://WRITER.com.



📐 About the role

Join WRITER's security team as a staff detection and response engineer and help protect the AI infrastructure that's transforming how the world works. You'll build sophisticated detection systems that identify attacks targeting our AI platform, training data, and model deployments while creating automated response capabilities that scale with our explosive growth. This isn't just traditional security work – you're defending cutting-edge AI/AGI systems against adversaries who are evolving their tactics as fast as AI itself advances.

This role combines hands-on security engineering with strategic thinking to stay ahead of novel threats that don't exist in textbooks yet. You'll be the operational arm of our security function, translating threat intelligence into real-time detections, coordinating incident response across multiple teams, and hunting for sophisticated attacks across GPU clusters and distributed training environments. If you're excited by the challenge of securing systems that are fundamentally different from anything you've protected before, this is your opportunity to define what AI security engineering looks like at scale.

You'll work closely with our AI Security research team, Cloud Infrastructure, Software Security Engineering, and AI researchers to build a defense-in-depth strategy that protects one of the most valuable AI platforms in the industry. The threats are real, the stakes are high, and the problems are intellectually fascinating.

This role can be based in San  reporting to our head of security operations.



🦸🏻‍♀️ What you’ll do

 - Design and implement detection strategies that identify AI-specific threats including prompt injection, model extraction, data poisoning, adversarial examples, and unauthorized access to training datasets or model weights across our distributed infrastructure

 - Build automated response playbooks and orchestration workflows that contain threats without human intervention, creating self-healing security systems that reduce mean time to response from hours to minutes while automatically remediating compromised inference endpoints

 - Lead security incident response coordination across all teams (Cloud, AppSec, Enterprise, AI Security) when AI infrastructure or models are compromised, conducting forensic investigations on training pipeline attacks and model manipulation attempts while drafting clear incident communications for engineering and executive leadership

 - Hunt proactively for sophisticated threats across GPU clusters and training infrastructure by analyzing model outputs for signs of compromise, reproducing AI-specific vulnerabilities from security research, and identifying visibility gaps in distributed training environments before adversaries exploit them

 - Build detection-as-code frameworks with version control and automated deployment, onboard telemetry from AI training infrastructure and inference endpoints, and create dashboards that track model security metrics, GPU utilization patterns, and access to sensitive research data

 - Collaborate cross-functionally as the operational security partner for all teams – translating AI Security's threat research into production detections, monitoring Cloud Infrastructure's GPU clusters for threats, detecting customer-impacting incidents for Software Security Engineering, and enabling responsible AI development through security guardrails

 - Maintain 24/7 on-call rotation for critical AI security incidents, responding to real-time threats targeting our platform while continuously improving detection coverage and automation capabilities as our AI systems evolve



⭐️ What you need

 - 3-5+ years in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response with a proven track record of identifying and stopping sophisticated attacks in production environments, plus 3+ years specifically securing AI/ML infrastructure, high-performance computing environments, or other distributed systems at scale

 - Strong programming skills in Python, KQL, SPL, or similar languages that allow you to build custom detection logic, automate response workflows, and create tools that operationalize security at scale across cloud-native and distributed computing environments

 - Experience with SIEM platforms, detection technologies, and forensic investigation techniques with demonstrated ability to build detection for novel attack techniques that don't have established patterns yet and to conduct forensics in complex distributed environments

 - Self-directed execution mindset with a track record of securing high-value intellectual property, automating incident response in complex environments, and identifying critical security gaps through proactive threat hunting before they become incidents

 - Deep alignment with WRITER's values – you naturally Connect across security, infrastructure, and AI research teams to build comprehensive defenses, you Challenge assumptions about what's possible in AI security engineering, and you Own the protection of our AI platform with unwavering accountability and a commitment to staying ahead of evolving threats

ABOUT YOU The Xsolla Offerwall puts rewarded offers in front of players inside the games and apps of our publishers. A player opens the wall, picks an offer, completes it, and earns in-game currency. Whether they do depends on what they see: the offer card, the creative, the video, the playable, and the reward moment. Those units come from several places. Some are native offers we render ourselves. Some arrive as VAST video, HTML or MRAID creatives, or OpenRTB Native assets from demand partners. Each format has its own rules, and each one has to look right in a publisher's game, on a phone, without breaking what the advertiser sent. You'll own how offerwall ads look and perform. You'll decide which formats we support and how they render. You'll design what the player sees, and turn that into specs engineers can build from. You'll measure whether a change made players more likely to engage, and you'll use AI to make better creative faster than a manual process allows. ABOUT US Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game. For more information, visit xsolla.com.           Responsibilities:

Ad experience and creative

  • Own the look and feel of every ad unit in the offerwall: offer cards, detail pages, video, playables, interstitials, and the reward flow.

  • Set creative standards for advertisers and publishers: layouts, asset specs, safe areas, aspect ratios, and branding rules.

  • Balance three groups who want different things: players want a clean experience, publishers want it to match their game, and advertisers want their brand shown properly.

    • oRTB formats and rendering

  • Define how we support VAST, HTML and MRAID, and OpenRTB Native inside the offerwall, across Web, iOS, Android, and Unity.

  • Write the requirements for format support: which VAST events we track, which MRAID calls we allow, and how Native assets map into our own templates.

  • Work with Engineering on creative QA and rejection rules, so broken or non-compliant creatives get caught before a player sees them.

    • Design to engineering

  • Turn ideas into Figma designs and prototypes that engineers can build without guessing.

  • Write PRDs and acceptance criteria that cover states, edge cases, and device differences, not just the happy path.

  • Work with our designers on the offerwall's design system, and keep it consistent across publishers and platforms.

    • Experimentation and performance

  • Run A/B tests on layouts, creative treatments, and formats, and read the results yourself.

  • Track the metrics that show whether the ad experience works: CTR, video completion rate, offer start and completion rates, IPM, and eCPM.

  • Turn what you learn into a prioritized roadmap, and explain the tradeoffs to Engineering, Demand, and leadership.

    • AI in creative and workflow

  • Find where AI can improve ad units: generating creative variants, adapting assets to new formats, auto-cropping and localization, and checking creative quality.

  • Use AI tools in your own work: prototyping, writing specs, analyzing test results, and getting from idea to something testable faster.

    • Cross-functional work

  • Work with Engineering, Design, Demand, Publisher Success, and Data every week.

  • Give the Demand team clear creative guidelines they can share with advertisers.

  • Bring what publishers and advertisers say back into the roadmap, in a form engineers can act on.

    • Qualifications & Skills:

  • Around 5 years of product management experience, with a significant part of it in AdTech.

  • Hands-on experience owning ad design or ad experience: ad units, creative formats, or how ads render in an app or game.

  • Working knowledge of oRTB ad formats. You know how VAST, HTML and MRAID, and OpenRTB Native creatives work, what breaks them, and what the specs allow.

  • Comfortable with data. You can design an A/B test, read the result, and write SQL or use a BI tool to answer your own questions.

  • You write clear specs. Engineers should be able to build from what you write without coming back to ask what you meant.

  • Good visual judgment. You can tell why one layout works and another doesn't, and explain it in terms of player behavior.

  • Clear communication with engineers, designers, and commercial teams.

  • Based in Los Angeles or elsewhere in the US, and able to work across US time zones.

    • Nice to Have:
  • Experience working with AI. This one matters a lot to us. Show us how you've used AI tools such as Claude, Midjourney, or Figma AI to make ads, prototype products, or get more done. Come ready to show a real example.
  • Experience with offerwalls, rewarded ads, or rewarded video.
  • Experience designing in Figma: building prototypes and engineering-ready designs yourself, not just reviewing someone else's.
  • Experience in mobile gaming or app monetization.
  • Familiarity with ad SDKs, mediation, and how they render third-party creatives.
    • What Your Week Looks Like:

  • A demand partner starts sending VAST wrappers that time out on Android. You look at the VAST chain, work out where it's slow, and agree a timeout and fallback rule with Engineering.

  • Offer completion rates on one publisher are 30% below the network average. You compare their wall against others, find the reward value is hidden below the fold on smaller phones, and mock up a fix in Figma that afternoon.

  • An advertiser wants to run a playable in the offerwall. You check what their MRAID creative needs, decide what we'll support, and write the spec.

  • You use an AI image model to generate 20 variants of an offer card's hero image, test four of them, and share the winner and the lift with the team.

  • Engineering asks how Native title and icon assets should behave when an advertiser sends nothing. You answer the same day, with the rule written into the spec.

    • How Success Is Measured:

  • Offerwall engagement improves: higher CTR, offer start rate, and completion rate, backed by test results rather than claims.

  • The formats we support render correctly across platforms, and creative rejections and rendering bugs go down.

  • Engineering builds from your specs and designs without long back-and-forth.

  • Advertisers and publishers have clear creative guidelines, and the Demand team uses them.

  • AI is part of how the team makes and tests creative, not a side experiment.

ABOUT SUPABASE

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We're hiring a Product Manager for Supabase Realtime https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime. You'll own the surface area developers use to build live, collaborative and event-driven apps on Supabase: Broadcast https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/broadcast, Presence https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/presence, Postgres Changes https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/postgres-changes, and the capabilities we build next.

You'll work closely with the Realtime Engineering team and with partners across Product Management, Design and GTM.

This role is ideal for someone who's excited about building tools for millions of developers and who has a passion for the types of user experiences unlocked by simple, scalable real-time channels. You should have a nuanced understanding of full-stack application development, including existing and emerging real-time and sync patterns.



WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - You'll own the problem statements and solution rationale behind the Realtime roadmap. This means working with Engineering and Design to shape how Supabase crafts the developer experience for the problems you’ve prioritized solving.

 - You'll shape how Realtime evolves to enable future application experiences, including its role in AI apps and alongside other Supabase products.

 - You'll own Realtime packaging and pricing, working with Pricing, Finance and Billing.

 - You'll use data to understand how Supabase developers are using Realtime features: where they succeed, where they get stuck, and what to tackle first.

 - You'll keep Engineering, Design and GTM aligned. You'll own the plan of record for what's coming, why, and in what order.
   


YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU


MUST HAVE

 - 5+ years of Product Management experience on developer tools, or are an ex-founder with equivalent depth. You're comfortable commenting on an architecture doc, following a design discussion, and advocating for the user when trade-offs are required.

 - Have owned an app development platform, feature or framework where real-time was core to the developer experience.

 - Get your own answers from data. You know what you care about in terms of product instrumentation and are comfortable querying and cleaning your own findings.

 - Are comfortable with Postgres and familiar with logical replication.

 - Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote. You make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.
   


STRONG SIGNAL

 - You have an existing audience among developers, through social media, open source or developer advocacy.

 - Worked on a sync engine, local-first or live-query product.

 - Worked with gaming, AR or collaborative-tool customers.

 - Shipped something using Supabase.


WHAT WE OFFER

   We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

   Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

 - Tech Allowance
   
   Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

 - Health Benefits
   
   Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

   Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

   We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

 - Professional Development
   
   Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.
   
   


ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

 - ~400 team members

 - 60+ countries

 - 20+ languages spoken

 - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

 - 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

  • Unearth insights through advanced analytics and data exploration across billions of transactions to inform product strategy and development

We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.

We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts.  - Build the infrastructure for reproducible agent environments where models can interact with documents, tools, and external systems during training and evaluation.

 - Own the performance and reliability of training runs, including GPU utilization, checkpointing, failure recovery, and observability.

 - Identify and remove bottlenecks across training and inference to shorten the path from research idea to useful result.

Hi, I’m Kayla https://www.linkedin.com/in/kayla-ricketts-9727976b/ :) I lead global community activation within Partnerships at Ashby. We’re hiring an experienced TA Expert & Community Lead in AMER to help expand one of our most successful GTM experiments: a high-touch, customer-led approach to growth. The model is already working in EMEA, built on curated events, product education and early community activation.—to create meaningful impact across the funnel. This role suits someone who has worked with Ashby All-in-One, has a solid background in TA, and cares about tools, process, hospitality and community building. It also works well for TA people who still love the work but want to use what they know somewhere new. You’ll work closely with Sales, CS and Product Marketing, own a region end-to-end, and see how community connects to pipeline and retention.

A quick summary on travel, since it’s usually the first question, and we know it means time away from home: you’ll have events around twice a month, usually for around four days. We plan the calendar well in advance, so you’ll know what’s coming and can sort things at home with plenty of notice.

It’s also one of the best parts of the job. I’ve met some amazing people and had some really cool experiences along the way, from hosting a dinner cruise on the Seine  https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ashbyhq_last-night-we-spent-a-great-evening-with-activity-7518934121507913728-51U1?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAAA7jUaYB2IctkRuC7u91bcl_fuRCHV_o-w8and a TA leader workshop with a partner https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7519293611298131968 at the Shangri-La Paris, to spending time in customers’ offices https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7519293611298131968 in Stockholm, our company offsite  https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7516557949570412544in Playa Del Carmen, and hosting the mainstage at our first Ashby One London. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7503489909475876864



What you’ll do

 - Lead AMER Community Events
   
   - Run community events across target AMER markets. Event types might include:
     
     - Customer learning breakfasts
     
     - A mixed ecosystem event for customers and prospects
     
     - Partner cocktail events or roundtables co-hosted with local ecosystem players
   
   - Build and nurture relationships with TA leaders
   
   - Partner with Event Ops on venue selection, invites, and post-event recaps
   
   - Drive improvement and reimagine how we can show up in a very meaningful way for the community

 - Drive Customer Education
   
   - Become an Expert in Ashby + TA leader needs to curate relevant content
   
   - Design and lead live sessions that help customers activate key Ashby features and keep customers ahead on key TA trends and topics
   
   - Partner with CS and Product Marketing teams on the Ashby Hidden Gems program
   
   - Develop and distribute product tips, dashboards, and templates to increase customer sophistication

 - Expand AMER Community and Customer Advocacy
   
   - Help Ashby deepen its brand and trust by showing up consistently and thoughtfully
   
   - Develop onboarding and enablement loops for ACE (Ashby Customer Expert) events
   
   - Partner with GTM teams on prospect and customer onsite visits
   
   - Moderate panels, attend events, and build a presence at industry gatherings



Who you’ll work with

You’ll report directly to me, but work closely with Willem https://www.linkedin.com/in/willemwijnans/ and the EMEA community team, who’ve pioneered what community growth looks like at Ashby. Within partnerships, you’ll also work closely with Katie https://www.linkedin.com/in/katherineelainecampbell/ to scale trusted community partner relationships and our Event Ops team on bringing Owned Community experiences, like Ashby Cafe https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7478334221007294465, to life.


About You

We think the ideal person for this role will have experience and skills that look something like this:

 - You’ve been an Ashby power user or at least very familiar with Ashby and seen its benefits first-hand—someone who knows the product and Ashby community, champions good recruiting practices, and isn’t afraid to dive into dashboards, workflows, or templates

 - You’ve built a reputation inside organizations as the go-to expert on TA process and tooling

 - You’re a strong communicator—whether facilitating a breakfast, writing a post-event summary, or helping a customer understand how to build a dashboard

 - You love curating and connecting people and ideas. You get energy from hosting, matchmaking, and finding smart formats to share what works

 - You’re excited about being on the road ~2x/month and tapping into your existing network (and growing it!) in the TA space

 - You have strong business acumen. You understand how community supports the wider business and work well with Sales and CS to make sure our programs are reaching the right people

 - You’re entrepreneurial and experimental in nature. You’re not looking for rigid playbooks; you want room to try new formats and evolve what ‘great’ looks like. You come prepared with AI tools / automations that help us execute faster while maintaining quality.

 - You believe in unreasonable hospitality—the idea that going above and beyond for a customer doesn’t just build goodwill, it builds momentum.

This Role Probably Isn't Right If ...

 - You’re not excited about hosting or don’t enjoy the details of curating small, thoughtful gatherings

 - You hate writing and have difficulty building a cohesive brief (this is a very important skill at Ashby)

 - You don’t enjoy travelling and building new connections while you’re at it

 - You’ve never had hands-on TA experience

 - You’ve never used Ashby and aren’t familiar with modern TA systems and practices

 - You prefer working from a very established playbook and are uncomfortable with ambiguity or iteration

 - You’re uncomfortable with moderating discussions or being a speaker

 - You only have an ‘events background’. For this role, we need folks with deep knowledge of the TA ecosystem and a proven network in major city hubs like San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles, Seattle, Boston, Austin, and Chicago

Interview Plan

 - Recruiter Screen with Michelle - 30 minutes

 - Hiring Manager Interview with Kayla - 45 minutes

 - Cross-functional Panel - 1 hour

 - Assignment (written) - 2 hours
   
   - Followed by Assignment Review with Kayla - 30 Minutes

 - Final Round - 1-1.5 hours

Kin makes life simpler, more affordable, and better for homeowners — especially in the places where climate risks, rising costs, and outdated systems make it hardest. We start with smarter homeowners insurance and expand to everything homeowners need to thrive.

Its programs span thousands of people, multiple organizations, billion-dollar budgets, and differentiated security environments. We’re changing that. Morgan, and built software that operates across government and commercial environments, from unclassified work to Top Secret networks.

OUR SOLUTION

Integrate gives complex programs something they have never had before. One real-time schedule that can operate across organizations, security boundaries, and classification levels without fragmenting the schedule.

The program stays live as it changes. Teams can see how the program has moved, understand how a change ripples downstream, surface risk before it compounds, and control access down to the individual element. And our AI architecture works from that same continuously updated program state. It understands what is happening now, not a report assembled days or weeks ago. The schedule stops being a static plan and becomes a living reflection of the program itself.

We’re nowhere near done. We want to set a new standard for how the world’s most complex work gets done, and we won’t stop until we do.
